name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,561

clue.text: Plane that sounds like a submarine perhaps?

indicators.note: sounds like says the word before it is to be heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: to plane wood is to smooth it, as is to sand it
that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns; the spoken word is spelt without its H

explanation.surface: An aircraft whose engine noise reminds someone of a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft but is the verb for smoothing wood. A submarine, or sub, is a long filled bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine roll is a well-known variety of the filled-bread snack, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: How pool winners do it?

blocks.note: surface reading: the way champions of the cue game pool play their matches
setter's reading: winners in a swimming pool succeed by moving through water, and the adverb also means very smoothly and successfully

explanation.surface: A question about how champions at the pool table secure their victories.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool suggests the cue game, but here it is a swimming pool; the answer is an adverb meaning very well, built on what swimmers do.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means smoothly and successfully, and literally describes racers moving through water in a bath.

clue.text: Catch gentleman's shot in snooker club

indicators.note: to catch something said is to hear it, so the words that follow are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a knight is a titled gentleman; the silent K drops out when spoken
a pot is a shot that sinks a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: Someone at a snooker club watches a titled gentleman make a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT'S POT, said aloud, is NIGHTSPOT. 'In snooker club' reads as one place, but 'in' joins the wordplay to the definition 'club'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub or venue for evening entertainment, so it fits the noun for a dancing venue.

clue.text: Moderate politicians coming from troublesome situation up North

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up towards the north means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be in a state of worry or difficulty

explanation.surface: Centrist politicians emerge from some awkward trouble in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Wets was Margaret Thatcher's label for moderate Conservatives who opposed her harder policies.
explanation.definitionFit: In British political slang the plural noun names mild, centrist party members regarded as lacking firmness.

clue.text: Has an inclination to enter church free from sin

indicators.note: one piece going in to enter another means it sits inside that other piece

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
something with an inclination tilts or leans

explanation.surface: Someone feels drawn towards entering a church to be purged of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purify, and spiritual purification removes moral wrongdoing from a person.

clue.text: Digs sunglasses Henry traded in for Penny

indicators.note: trading one thing in for another swaps it out, so one letter is removed and the other put in its place

blocks.note: shades is informal for sunglasses
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a pair of sunglasses belonging to Henry for a penny coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The H in SHADES is replaced by P. 'Digs' looks like lodgings but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To spade the earth is to turn soil with a garden tool, which is exactly what excavating it means.

clue.text: Hurry beyond Little Rock for outside covering

indicators.note: beyond places the first-named piece further along, after the second one

blocks.note: a pebble is a small stone
to dash is to hurry

explanation.surface: A traveller rushes past the Arkansas city of Little Rock in search of a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Rock looks like the American city, but it is simply a small stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pebbledash is an exterior render for house walls with small stones pressed into the mortar.

clue.text: Prosecutor on TV standing up for courts

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits on top of it, so it comes first
in a down entry, standing up turns the word so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
a TV set is a television

explanation.surface: A prosecutor appears on television standing up for the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law courts, but it is the verb meaning woos.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them romantically, and going out with a sweetheart is the same idea.

clue.text: Breakers from Soviet Union's Russian Federation leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: The heads of the Soviet Union and the Russian Federation are portrayed as rule-breakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakers are large waves crashing on a shore, and that white foaming water is what surfers ride.

clue.text: Some loathe media having a recurring motif

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some people hate media coverage that keeps repeating the same pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built around a repeated idea or subject is organised on a theme throughout.

clue.text: Expensive bar serving otherworldly bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so the phrase holds the wanted letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A pricey bar stocks bottles of an unearthly drink for its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Expensive bar looks like a posh pub; it is a bar of metal, and 'bottles' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast block of gold or silver, a costly bar of precious metal.

clue.text: Alarmingly, boxer hit international expo participant

indicators.note: something done alarmingly causes disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A boxer startlingly punches a delegate at an international trade fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a trade show, and those who display wares on stands there are its showers of goods.

clue.text: Couple from China

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to pair up or breed
second meaning: Cockney rhyming slang, china plate standing for a friend

explanation.surface: A pair of travellers arrive from China.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means a pal, so 'my old china' is my friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pairing off to breed and a British informal noun for a friend or pal.

clue.text: Suspect mailman is into carnality

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not to be trusted in their given order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dubious postman is suspected of indulging in fleshly desires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a noun about the mailman, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Animalism means devotion to bodily appetites and physical urges, the same as fleshly sensuality.

clue.text: Fruitcake talks of trendy hair-style

indicators.note: talks of means the words are spoken, so their sound counts rather than their spelling

blocks.note: current means up to date or fashionable, and it sounds like the dried fruit
a bun is hair coiled into a knot at the back of the head

explanation.surface: An eccentric person chatters about a fashionable hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' suggests an eccentric person; here it is literal. A currant bun is a sweet British bread roll studded with dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant bun is a small sweet baked roll dotted with dried grapes, so it is literally a fruited cake.

clue.text: American man on street upset Girl Guides

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first
to upset something is to knock it over and into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: US is short for American
he is the pronoun for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American man in the street annoys a troop of Girl Guides.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl Guides looks like the youth organisation; here it means women who guide, as in a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Usherettes are women who show people to their seats in a cinema or theatre, so they are female guides.

clue.text: Priest caught in trap by a French heavenly body

indicators.note: something caught in a thing is held inside it
by means next to, so the following piece is placed alongside

blocks.note: a net is a trap for catching things
P is short for priest
une is the French for a, feminine

explanation.surface: A priest is snared in a trap beside a beautiful French woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the eighth planet from the sun, and planets are celestial bodies.

clue.text: They avoid barking red dogs

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and mad letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People steer clear of noisy ginger dogs that keep yapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the noise dogs make; in British slang it also means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgers are people who evade or sidestep things, so 'they avoid' describes them as a group.

clue.text: European motorbike company supported by viable training

indicators.note: in a down entry, something supported by another sits on top of it, so it comes first

blocks.note: E is short for European
Ducati is an Italian motorcycle maker
on means possible or feasible, as in 'that is not on'

explanation.surface: A European motorcycle firm is backed by a sound training programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Education is the process of teaching and instruction, which is what training provides.

clue.text: Lo-cal treacle taken regularly, as stated on the tin

indicators.note: taken at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

blocks.note: lite is the labelling term for low-calorie food
the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Low-calorie syrup is eaten at intervals, exactly as the label instructs.
explanation.walkthrough: Treacle is a dark sugar syrup. 'Does what it says on the tin' is a British phrase for something exactly as described.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal means exactly as the words say, without exaggeration, which is what the idiom about the tin label conveys.

clue.text: After economy with the truth mean to keep quiet

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the first one in reading order

blocks.note: being economical with the truth is a euphemism for telling an untruth
low means base or mean in character

explanation.surface: Having been economical with the truth, it's mean to stay silent too.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for keeping out of sight and drawing no attention, staying discreetly hidden.

clue.text: Enterprise, reorganising, must face Eastern outfit

indicators.note: reorganising puts things into a different order, so the following word's letters are rearranged
to face something is to stand in front of it, so these letters come before the next piece

blocks.note: an enterprise is a business, a company, abbreviated CO
taken as written
E is short for Eastern

explanation.surface: A business undergoing restructuring has to confront an Eastern rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reorganising' sounds like corporate restructuring of the enterprise, but it acts only on 'must'.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes worn together, especially for a performance, so it is an ensemble of garments.

clue.text: What chef did outside recipe is not kosher

indicators.note: one piece placed outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: a chef's job is to prepare food with heat
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A chef strays from the recipe, so the dish no longer meets Jewish dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not kosher' suggests forbidden food in a kitchen; it is the informal sense of not honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Not kosher is informal for dishonest or dodgy, and crooked describes fraudulent, underhand dealing.

clue.text: Bum shilling for animated character who’s lost his trousers

definitions.text: animated character who’s lost his trousers

blocks.note: to bum something is to cadge it, to scrounge or sponge
bob is slang for a shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure has lost his trousers and is offering his backside for a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The character is SpongeBob SquarePants, so dropping his 'pants' (trousers) from the name leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon sea sponge's full name ends in SquarePants; without that surname, only his first two names remain.

clue.text: Board's main political principle

blocks.note: first meaning: a long flat piece of timber
second meaning: a key policy in a party's platform

explanation.surface: A company board's central political stance is set out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a long length of sawn timber and a single central policy within a party platform.

clue.text: Gesture with a heartless vote

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle, leaving just its outside letters

blocks.note: W is short for with
taken as written
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone raises a hand to cast a cold, uncaring vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave is a motion of the hand in greeting or farewell, a kind of bodily signal.

clue.text: Sourpuss runs in Hackney

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following piece

blocks.note: a hackney carriage is the official name for a London taxi
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A grumpy person goes jogging in the London borough of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough; it is the hackney carriage, a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is an irritable, bad-tempered person, the same as a grouch or misery.

clue.text: First husband exposed by topless minx

indicators.note: without a top, the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: a madam is a cheeky, precocious girl, as is a minx

explanation.surface: A woman's first husband is shown up by a saucy girl without her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First husband' looks like someone's ex; it is the Biblical first man, husband of Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the original man was married to Eve, making him the earliest husband of all.

clue.text: Barrier caused by unusually drab old rugby player

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters appear in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
O is short for old
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: An obstruction was created by a strangely dull veteran rugby forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is an obstruction set across a street to stop traffic, so it is an obstacle.

clue.text: Tendancy of medic providing end to treatment

definitions.note: misspelt in the original clue for 'tendency'

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: Dr is short for doctor
providing means on condition that, as does if
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor brings a course of treatment to its close.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift is the general direction or gist of something, the way it is inclined to move.

clue.text: Atoll where one pursues lovingly flexible relations

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the others

blocks.note: bi is short for bisexual, attracted to more than one sex
kin are one's relatives
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An island where one person chases relationships of a loose, open kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini Atoll in the Pacific was the site of US nuclear tests, and gave its name to the swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a ring-shaped coral island in the Marshall Islands, a real Pacific reef group.

clue.text: Scraps rum before crew starts to turn seditious

indicators.note: before puts the first piece in front of what follows
the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
a crew is a body of men
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A drunken ship's company turns against its captain, ditching the rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink; in British slang it means peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover bits and pieces, remnants that remain, which is what scraps are.
